chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from al-Kahili, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him: 'A house was shared among a group of people, and they left a courtyard between them in which is their passage. Then a man came and bought the share of one of them. Is that permissible for him?' He said: 'Yes, but he must close his door and open a door to the road, or descend from above the house. If their partner wishes to sell the passage of his feet, then they have more right to it. And if he wishes, he comes until he sits on the closed door that he sold, and they cannot prevent him.'

key_terms.مَنْقَلَ قَدَمَيْهِ: The passage of his feet (right of way)

ai.seo_question: What are the rights of a new co-owner in a shared property regarding access and passage according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the mechanics of *Shuf'ah* (pre-emption) in shared real estate, emphasizing that a new co-owner acquires full rights to the physical structure, including the ability to seal off the old shared entrance if they choose. This ruling highlights the balance between individual property rights and communal access, a key principle in Shia jurisprudence regarding joint ownership (*Musha*). The hadith further stipulates that if a partner wishes to sell their share, the remaining co-owners have the primary right of first refusal, reinforcing the social cohesion of shared properties.
